summary: The agent successfully manipulated PPTX files by working directly with the Open XML format. Key learnings: (1) Python's zipfile module is the reliable way to extract/repackage PPTX when unzip is unavailable, (2) PPTX is a ZIP archive with XML files that can be directly edited for precise control over formatting, (3) EMU units (914400 per inch) are used for positioning and sizing, (4) slide relationships and Content_Types.xml must be kept consistent when adding slides. The task failed verification despite appearing correct, suggesting the need for validation scripts and understanding of test expectations.

The agent successfully completed PPTX XML manipulation but encountered several friction points: (1) ET.register_namespace failed with reserved prefixes, forcing fallback to regex/string manipulation, (2) multiple tool call errors with extra spaces in function names (' Read'), (3) truncated bash output required workarounds, (4) the agent used python-pptx style thinking but had to drop to raw XML. The existing pptx-xml-manipulation skill covers basic structure but lacks practical patterns for text formatting modifications, namespace-safe editing techniques, and defensive bash practices. Updating the skill with these patterns will help future agents avoid the same pitfalls.

The trace shows the agent successfully used the existing pptx-xml-manipulation skill to clean up trail-stop captions. The agent made good decisions: using regex-based string replacement instead of xml.etree.ElementTree (as the skill recommends), extracting to /tmp, and building the new slide from scratch. The failure appears to be unrelated to the PPTX manipulation itself—the agent completed the work and the output file was created. Key observations: 1) The skill's anti-pattern guidance about string replacement vs ET was followed correctly, 2) The agent had minor issues with extra spaces in tool names (' Bash' vs 'Bash') which the skill already warns about, 3) The slide addition workflow in the skill was followed correctly. No substantive skill updates needed—the existing skill adequately guided the agent. Minor addition: clarifying that split text runs (multiple <a:r> elements for one caption) need special handling when doing text replacement.

The task involved cleaning up location captions in a PowerPoint presentation using python-pptx. The trace reveals several recurring issues that need documentation: (1) python-pptx naming quirks (RGBColor not RgbColor, _Paragraph has no getparent), (2) checking for NoneColor before accessing .rgb, (3) opaque XML handling for numbered lists via lxml elements, (4) proper venv setup patterns for isolated package installation, and (5) the agent making repeated tool call errors due to leading spaces in function names. The existing pptx-xml-manipulation skill covers direct XML editing, but there's a gap for python-pptx high-level API usage with its common pitfalls and workarounds.

The agent successfully completed a PPTX caption cleanup task but encountered multiple pitfalls that are highly reusable: python-pptx installation issues in externally-managed environments, RGBColor capitalization errors, _NoneColor attribute errors when reading unset colors, float-to-int conversion failures for EMU positioning, and shape type detection failures. The trace also shows successful patterns for auto-numbered lists via XML manipulation. This skill update captures these failure modes and working patterns to help future agents avoid the same trial-and-error.

The trace reveals significant friction in PPTX manipulation: the agent struggled with precise caption positioning, width calculations per text length, duplicate shape handling, and content preservation. Key gaps include: (1) no reusable width estimation for single-line text, (2) no pattern for safely removing duplicate shapes while preserving originals, (3) missing verification that formatting actually applied to XML, (4) no script for batch caption standardization. The existing pptx-xml-manipulation skill covers basic extraction/editing but lacks these precision workflows. This patch adds a comprehensive caption-standardization skill with width estimation heuristics, safe shape deduplication patterns, and validation scripts.

Agent failed verifier despite claiming success. Key issues: (1) Used space-prefixed tool name ' Bash' causing tool error (line 1378), (2) Failed to properly handle split text runs in slide 5 initially, requiring multiple re-extractions, (3) Captions ended up concatenated with other text ('Photo Plate 01Street-market...') rather than isolated. Adding skill for robust PPTX split-text handling and tool name validation.

The task failed verifier tests despite apparent success. The trace reveals critical issues: (1) the agent used a leading space in tool name ' Bash' which failed immediately, (2) the color was set to #5B6776 instead of the required #6B7280 (gray-500), (3) the Inspection Index slide formatting verification showed auto-numbering but the actual structure may not match pytest expectations. The agent also showed iterative trial-and-error with partial matching logic for caption names that wasn't robust. This skill update adds a dedicated CSV-to-PPTX caption standardization skill with strict validation rules, correct color values, and explicit verification steps that would have caught these errors.
